A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Plan-R1 work. Their complete main texts, figures, tables, equations and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching retained material across pagination changes.

before.justification: v3 reports original nuPlan planning results, component and hyperparameter ablations, pass@k analysis and qualitative driving outcomes.

after.justification: v4 retains those empirical results and adds interPlan evaluation and frozen-world-model perturbation results in Tables 6–7.

M1.justification: The two-stage training procedure, dual-model architecture, rule-based rewards, VD-GRPO objective and inference procedure remain unchanged. Appendix E analyzes the existing method without establishing an algorithmic modification.

E1.justification: Coverage expands beyond standard nuPlan splits to interPlan scenes with altered agents, obstacles and goals, plus surrounding-agent prediction under corrupted ego observations. These introduce distinct environment and observation shifts relevant to the safety claims.

E2.justification: Comparator membership in the retained experiments is unchanged. The new interPlan comparison uses a subset of methods already compared in v3, including PLUTO, Diffusion Planner, IDM and PDM variants; no new comparison method is introduced.

E3.justification: Appendix B adds evaluation over all 335 interPlan scenarios and a controlled Gaussian perturbation protocol affecting historical and current ego states, with sigma values of 0, 0.1, 0.3, 1, 3 and 10 meters and surrounding-agent ADE/FDE metrics. Existing training and nuPlan evaluation settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New analyses test planning robustness under manipulated long-tail traffic and frozen-world-model sensitivity to ego-state deviations, addressing failure conditions absent from v3's experiments. Existing reward, capacity, world-model-choice, group-size, KL/scaling and pass@k analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. The new Gaussian-noise standard deviations specify experimental perturbations, rather than uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: Retained tables and quantitative plots preserve their results. New Table 6 reports interPlan scores of 56.64 for Plan-R1 versus PLUTO's 57.74 without post-processing, and 72.33 for Plan-R1* versus PDM-Closed*'s 69.64. Table 7 adds ADE/FDE values ranging from 1.03/3.01 meters without noise to 1.26/3.59 at sigma=10 meters. These are additional settings, not improvements over v3 scores.

T1.justification: New Appendix E introduces gradient derivations, reward-mixture definitions, three lemmas with proofs, and a conditional corollary comparing reward variances. It also develops arguments about fixed scaling and RL–KL balance. This substantially extends v3's mathematical treatment, although group indexing and reward-bound assumptions contain inconsistencies.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions and conclusion retain the same claims about principle-aligned planning, the two-stage dual-model framework, VD-GRPO and nuPlan performance. Added supporting experiments and theory do not redefine those core claims.

C2.justification: Appendix B newly attributes PLUTO's interPlan advantage to its augmentation strategy and world-model perturbation tolerance to surrounding-agent histories and map context, extending that interpretation to rollout stability. The new Ethics Statement explicitly emphasizes that validation is limited to simulation.

D1.justification: The new Reproducibility Statement expands the stated release beyond source code to model checkpoints, experiment scripts and the preprocessing pipeline. Appendix D's architecture, hyperparameters, hardware and inference details remain unchanged; external resource availability is only asserted by the PDFs.

R1.justification: v4 adds Hallgarten et al. (2024) for interPlan and Tang et al. (2025), RAP, while removing Liu et al. (2024), the behavioral-topology work. The substantive positioning relative to hybrid IL/RL methods and Dr.GRPO remains unchanged.

P1.justification: The main narrative is largely unchanged. v4 adds acknowledgement, LLM-use, ethics and reproducibility statements, renames Appendix B to Additional Results, and appends a structured theory appendix. These are localized extensions rather than extensive rewriting or reorganization.

P2.justification: v4 adds Tables 6–7 and redraws Figure 6 with clearer road and agent markings while retaining the same scenarios. Conference headers and pagination change, but existing main-text displays and appendix sensitivity plots retain their layouts.

improvement.justification: Tables 6–7 provide useful additional robustness evidence, including the condition where unrefined Plan-R1 trails PLUTO, and Figure 6 becomes more legible. These yield a limited net improvement. The theoretical addition is less reliable: Equation (9) computes temporal rather than cross-rollout group statistics, and Equation (14)'s unit-interval reward bound is not reconciled with Appendix C's weights, limiting confidence in the new formal justification.
